data.description:
## Observation (read-only, 2026-11-18 PST)
- `sweating-revolting-oriole` (b23c-8220-e09f-448a, created 2026-11-12 via MCP) is bound to REB-7142 (binding created 2026-11-12T14:33:41Z, Jira status Done).
- REB-7141 carries the identical summary, has a LOWER key than REB-7142 (so Jira created it first), status To Do, and was bound inbound at 2026-11-12T15:31:22Z as a new local ticket `jira-reb-7141` tagged `imported:reconciler-bootstrap`.
- So one local ticket produced two Jira issues: the first create was not recorded as the binding, a second create was, and the first issue came back inbound as a duplicate ticket.
- The closed bug `21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03` covers the same symptom on Jira DC (index lag in recover_pending). REB is a Jira Cloud project, so that fix's scope does not establish the Cloud path is covered.

## Not established
- Which pass created REB-7141 and why its key was not recorded (lost response, timeout, recover_pending search miss on Cloud). The reconciler's run logs for 2026-11-12 14:00-15:40Z have not been read.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The pass that created REB-7141 and the reason its binding was not recorded are identified from reconciler logs or bridge state.
- [ ] Either the Cloud create path is fixed with a regression test that drops the create response and asserts one issue results, or the cause is shown to be already fixed with the commit named.
data.title: Outbound create for sweating-revolting-oriole left an orphan Jira issue (REB-7141) that the reconciler re-imported as a duplicate ticket
